footnotes.text: The Smith family was concerned for Joseph’s older brother Alvin, who died several years before the Church was organized. See Larry C. Porter, “Alvin Smith: Reminder of the Fairness of God,”Ensign,Sept. 1978, 65–67.

Eventually all saving ordinances, including confirmations, were performed for the dead in temples. Endowments for the dead were first performed in 1877 in the St. George Utah Temple.

The Endowment House was a structure in Salt Lake City dedicated to performing some temple ordinances (including baptisms and endowments for the living) before the Salt Lake Temple was completed.
